name: CI/CD
note: Questions authored by Claude as practice material. Not sourced from your own notes or any official exam. Verify anything you doubt against the docs.

questions.q: Where do GitHub Actions workflow files live?
questions.why: They are YAML files in .github/workflows/.

questions.q: Which trigger lets you start a workflow by hand from the Actions tab?
questions.why: workflow_dispatch adds a Run workflow button.

questions.q: How should you provide an API token to a workflow?
options: Store it as a repository secret and reference ${{ secrets.NAME }}
Pass it in the commit message
questions.why: Secrets are encrypted and masked in logs.

questions.q: By default, how do jobs in one workflow run?
options: In parallel, unless one declares needs:
In random order, one at a time
questions.why: Use needs: to order jobs.

questions.q: What does runs-on select?
options: The runner machine type, such as ubuntu-latest
questions.why: It picks the runner image the job executes on.

questions.q: Which action keeps a test report so you can download it after the run?
questions.why: upload-artifact stores files from the run.

questions.q: Which trigger runs a workflow when a pull request is opened or updated?
questions.why: pull_request fires for PR events.

questions.q: What do Playwright tests usually need on a fresh CI runner before they run?
options: npx playwright install --with-deps to get browsers
questions.why: CI images may lack the browsers and system libraries.

questions.q: How does a workflow step make the whole run fail?
options: It exits with a non-zero exit code
It writes a file named fail
questions.why: Test runners return non-zero on failure and that fails the step.

questions.q: You want the report uploaded even when tests fail. What do you add to the upload step?
questions.why: if: always() runs the step regardless of earlier failures.

questions.q: What does CI stand for?
questions.why: Changes are merged and verified frequently by automation.

questions.q: What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
options: Delivery keeps code releasable with a manual release step; deployment releases automatically
questions.why: Both automate the path; deployment removes the manual gate.

questions.q: What is a pipeline?
options: An automated sequence of stages such as build, test and deploy
questions.why: Each stage can gate the next.

questions.q: What is a runner?
options: The machine that executes workflow jobs
questions.why: GitHub-hosted or self-hosted.

questions.q: Why does YAML indentation matter in a workflow file?
options: Indentation defines the structure; a wrong indent breaks or changes the workflow
questions.why: Use spaces, not tabs.

questions.q: What does a matrix strategy do?
options: Runs one job many times with different values such as browsers or versions
Makes the job faster by skipping tests
questions.why: For example, test on three Node versions.

questions.q: Why use actions/cache?
options: To reuse downloaded dependencies between runs and save time
questions.why: Cache key choice controls when it is refreshed.

questions.q: What is the difference between env and secrets in a workflow?
options: env holds plain variables visible in the file; secrets are encrypted and masked in logs
questions.why: Never put tokens in plain env values.

questions.q: In a step, what is the difference between uses and run?
options: uses runs a reusable action; run executes shell commands
run calls actions; uses runs shell
questions.why: For example uses: actions/checkout versus run: npm test.

questions.q: What does on: push: branches: [main] do?
options: Triggers on pushes to any branch
Triggers only on pushes to main
questions.why: Branch filters limit when the workflow runs.

questions.q: What does a reusable workflow need as its trigger?
questions.why: Other workflows call it with uses: ./.github/workflows/file.yml.

questions.q: What does a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress do?
options: Cancels an older run in the same group when a new one starts
questions.why: It stops wasted runs on repeated pushes.

questions.q: What do environments with required reviewers add?
options: A manual approval gate before a job that targets that environment
questions.why: Useful for deploys to shared environments.

questions.q: What does Playwright's retries setting help with?
options: Re-running failed tests, which also helps spot flaky ones
questions.why: A test that passes on retry should be reported as flaky and fixed.

questions.q: Why set permissions: for GITHUB_TOKEN in a workflow?
options: To grant only the access the workflow needs (least privilege)
questions.why: Smaller blast radius if a step is compromised.

questions.q: Why pin a third-party action to a commit SHA instead of a tag?
options: A tag can be moved to different code; a SHA is immutable
questions.why: It protects against a changed or compromised tag.

questions.q: How can one job pass a value to a later job?
questions.why: Declare outputs on the job, read them via needs.

questions.q: What does npx playwright test --shard=1/4 do?
options: Runs the first quarter of the test suite so shards can run in parallel on separate machines
questions.why: Sharding splits the suite across jobs to cut total time.
